(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Venkatesh Naik T) Miscellaneous First Appeal
No.101777/2021 is filed by the insurance company and Miscellaneous First Appeal No.100163/2021
is filed by the claimants aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 30.11.2020 passed by

the
learned
I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Jmfc, Ranebennur, in M.V.C. No.366/2019,

whereby
the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.41,32,000/- as compensation.

2.  For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
3.

Brief facts of the claimants' case before the Tribunal are that, on 17.12.2018, Chetan was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.04.JQ-9469 from Davanagere towards Bengaluru after attending a marriage at Davanagere with other friends.

The motorcycle was driven by Jagadeesh and when they reached near Sibara village in front of Kapra Petrol bunk at about 2:30 pm, one VRL goods lorry bearing registration No.MH-13-R-2922 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from back side and dashed to NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB the motorcycle.
Due to which, both the rider and the pillion fell down and the wheel of the lorry ran over Chetan and he sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
The claimants contended that deceased was aged about 22 years and was taking KAS coaching and had completed BE degree.
Hence, the claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, before the Tribunal seeking compensation.

4. After service of notice before the Tribunal, respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are the owner and insurer of the vehicle, respectively, appeared through their counsel and resisted the claim petition by filing written statement denying all the averments made in the claim petition.

5. The Tribunal considering the evidence on record at Exs.P1 to P44, oral evidence of PW1 and PW2,
RW1 and Ex.R1, awarded total compensation of Rs.41,32,000/- with interest at 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

6. Being aggrieved by the impugned order, the insurance company has preferred appeal seeking for reduction of the compensation and the claimants have sought for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB Smt. Anasuyamma W/O Parashuramappa vs M/S Managing Director on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22574024/

4 7. Learned counsel for the insurance company contended that the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation towards loss of dependency by taking the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- and further committed an error in deducting 1/3rd of the income towards personal expenses of the deceased instead of 50%, as the deceased Chetan was a bachelor.

The Tribunal erred in awarding interest on the compensation at 7% per annum and the same has to be reduced to 6% in view of the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 AND CONNECTED MATTERS DISPOSED OF ON 24.8.2020).

entities.text: MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he sought to allow the appeal by reducing the compensation reasonably.

8. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the deceased had completed his BE Degree and was taking KAS coaching and therefore, he had a bright future but the Tribunal without considering this aspect, has taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month which is on the lower side.

In support of his contention, the learned counsel has relied on the decisions of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB MFA No.3556/2008 (between Sri.
Pushpahas Sheeshgiri Kulkarni and M/s Kadamba Transport Corporation, State of Goa disposed of on 21.01.2013) and in MFA No.100273/2023 (MFA No.3556/2008 (between Smt. Sunanda and others and Husensab and another disposed of on 30.05.2024).

Further, relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.4911/2023 arising out of SLP (C) No.16447/2022 in the case of Bishnupriya Panda v. Basanti Manjari Mohanty and anr., the learned counsel contended that the Apex Court considering that the deceased, who was a student of 4th year of MBBS and was aged 21 years at the time of the accident, had taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.50,000/-
per month and added 40% of the same towards future prospects.

entities.text: Bishnupriya Panda v. Basanti Manjari Mohanty and anr.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he prayed that, this Court should also consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.50,000/- per month.
Thus, he prayed to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation reasonably.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the only point that arises for our consideration is:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB "Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or does it call for enhancement or reduction?"
10.
The Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, has rightly held that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence, we do not find any ground to reverse the finding of the Tribunal with regard to the negligence and liability.
11. In the claim petition, the claimants have shown the age of the deceased as 22 years as on the date of the accident.
Claimant Nos.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased and claimant No.3 is the sibling of the deceased.
Chetan, the deceased, had completed his BE degree and this aspect is not denied by the insurance company.

In order to prove that the deceased had completed BE degree,
claimant No.1 has examined herself as PW.1 and also examined one Manjunath, who is the friend and studying along with Chetan, as PW.2 and relied on Ex.P.13 to 15-study certificates, Ex.P-16 true copy of SSLC marks card, Exs.P-17 to 23 Diploma marks card, Exs.P-24 to 29- BE Civil Engineering marks card, Ex.P-32 Provisional NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB Degree Certificate, Ex.P-37 KPSC Smt. Anasuyamma W/O Parashuramappa vs M/S Managing Director on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22574024/
5 application form and Ex.P-38- KPSC Admit card.
The oral evidence coupled with these documentary evidence clearly establish that as on the date of the accident, the deceased had completed his BE Civil Engineering.

12. In respect of the accident that had occurred on 27.07.2013, the Supreme Court considering the educational qualification of the deceased as MBBS student and was aged about 21 years at the time of the accident, taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.50,000/- per month and added 40% towards future prospects
. In the instant case, Chetan died in a road traffic accident on 17.12.2018.

Hence, considering the ration laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is just and necessary to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.25,000/- per month and 40% of the same has to be added towards future prospects of the deceased.
Claimant Nos.1 and 3 are the dependents of the deceased.
The deceased was a bachelor, hence half of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses and the remaining half of the income has to be taken contribution to the family.

As per Sarala Verma & Others Vs.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB Delhi Transport Corporation & Another1 case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is '18'.
Thus, loss of dependency is re

As per the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram @ Churu Ram & Others2 and National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others3, claimant Nos.1 and 3 being the mother and sister of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, Rs.15,000/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Thus, in all, the claimants are entitled to modified compensation as under:
 Loss of dependency Rs.37,80,000/-
 Loss of consortium (Rs.40000x2) Rs. 80,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

------------------
 Total Rs.38,90,000/-

6  14.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.38,90,000/- as against Rs.41,32,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

15. So far as the contention of the insurance company that the Tribunal has awarded interest on the compensation at the rate of 7% per annum is concerned, in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE supra, the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 7% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.
Hence, the same is reduced to 6% per annum.
16. Accordingly, the point for consideration is answered partly in the affirmative.

17. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that claimant Nos.1 and 3 are entitled to total compensation of Rs.38,90,000/- as against Rs.41,32,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
c) Respondent/Insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
d) Draw modified award accordingly.
e) Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit and also send a copy of this judgment to the Tribunal concerned forthwith.
f) No order as to costs.

17. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that claimant Nos.1 and 3 are entitled to total compensation of Rs.38,90,000/- as against Rs.41,32,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:16558-DB interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
c) Respondent/Insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
e) Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit and also send a copy of this judgment to the Tribunal concerned forthwith.
f) No order as to costs.
